topics.label: Lecture introduction
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic provides administrative framing and context for the lecture on complement.

topics.label: Foundational principles and central role of C3
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics establish the basic functions, naming conventions, and central role of C3 cleavage that govern the complement system.

topics.label: Pathways of complement activation and trigger threshold
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics detail the three upstream pathways that activate complement and converge to reach the critical threshold on target surfaces.

topics.label: Downstream effector mechanisms of complement
topics.groupedBecause: These subtopics explain the primary effector outcomes that destroy pathogens once complement activation occurs.

topics.label: Host cell regulation of complement
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic explains the regulatory proteins and mechanisms that prevent active complement from damaging host tissues.

topics.label: Clinical consequences of complement deficiencies
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic analyzes how deficiencies in specific complement components manifest clinically as distinct infection and autoimmune risks.

topics.label: Pathogen evasion mechanisms and applications of Protein A
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic examines how pathogens evade complement destruction and how bacterial evasion factors are utilized in laboratory and clinical settings.

topics.label: Lecture conclusion and upcoming topic preview
topics.groupedBecause: This subtopic provides the concluding remarks for the session and previews the next lecture on the adaptive immune system.
